summary: OFFLINE last-trick auto-play (frontend TS engine useLocalGame.ts) verified end-to-end via Playwright on live preview. Human's last card is auto-played without any tap, hand-end modal appears after the trick rest+collect, non-last tricks still require the human tap (regression OK), and Continuer transitions to the next hand.
test_report_links: Playwright script embedded in this iteration (see console output above); results:
Run A (H90 forced, all 7 tricks played manually): my hand 1->0 at t=5.68s WITHOUT any tap, hand-end-modal at t=8.78s.

Run B (with regression check): hand=2 waited 3s -> still 2 cards (no auto-play on non-last trick). Then hand 1->0 at t=3.45s WITHOUT any tap, modal at t=7.67s (gap 4.22s ~= 1s hold + 1s collect + 2.25s handEndReady). Continuer works: next hand starts with 8 cards (Donne 2).
critical_code_review_comments: useLocalGame.ts scheduleAuto: `lastTrickAuto = phase === 'playing' && hands[actor].length === 1` correctly scopes auto-play to the last trick only; humans on tricks 1-7 remain untimed (verified: hand=2 waited 3s, stayed 2).
Delay formula `pause + 1` (deterministic 1.0s) for last-trick auto matches backend cadence; bot moves on regular turns still use `pause + 1 + random()` — good separation.
app/game/[id].tsx: yourTurn sound correctly suppressed when hand.length===1 (line 271) so no chime fires when the human's last card is about to be auto-played.
TrickArea HOLD_MS=1000 matches the [id].tsx trick_end timers (950/2150) and handEndReady=2250 — timings consistent with observed 4.22s gap between last-card and modal.
engine.ts remains unchanged; scheduleAuto layer alone drives the new behavior. Clean separation.
